disclaimer.normal_residence: Exchange usually requires that you were normally resident in the issuing country when (and often while) you held the licence, and that you are resident in the destination when you exchange. EU law defines normal residence as living in a place for at least 185 days in each calendar year (Directive 2006/126/EC Art. 12). The Netherlands RDW states the same 185-day rule explicitly for non-EU/EFTA licences. A licence obtained without meeting that condition is often void in the destination.
disclaimer.scope: Lawful exchange conditions only. This is not a guide to licence tourism.
disclaimer.coverage: Seeded destinations: Germany (Anlage 11 FeV), Great Britain (Exchangeable Licences Orders), Netherlands (RDW agreement list), France (May 2026 non-EU reciprocity list), Ireland (recognised states). EU/EEA mutual recognition is not expanded as third-country annex rows.

destinations.name: United Kingdom (Great Britain)
destinations.instrument: Driving Licences (Exchangeable Licences) Orders — SI 1999/1641 (as amended) and SI 2021/537
notes: Applies to Great Britain (England, Wales, Scotland). Northern Ireland has a separate designation regime.
Exchange requires the applicant to be resident in GB and to meet DVLA exchange conditions; designation is not a fly-in product.
EU/EEA licences follow separate recognition/exchange rules and are not listed as "designated country" origins here.
Canada: SI 1999/1641 art. 4 designates Canadian provinces and territories — treat as subnational variance at country level.
Class correspondence is order-specific; this seed records designation (exchange without driving test) without inventing class maps.

destinations.name: Netherlands
destinations.instrument: RDW — Exchanging a foreign driving licence (countries outside EU/EFTA with agreement)
notes: EU/EFTA licences exchange under separate mutual rules (not listed as third-country agreement rows).
For non-EU/EFTA licences, RDW requires the holder lived in the issuing country for 185 days in the year the licence was obtained.
Exchange requires registration in the Dutch BRP (Personal Records Database) and other RDW conditions.
30% ruling expats may exchange a licence from any country under a separate scheme — not modelled as a general annex row.
